chunks: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud from Muhammad ibn Nusayr from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who has a predominant urge to urinate or defecate should perform ablution (wudu) during his prayer, and then complete the remainder of his prayer.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْبَطْنِ الْغَالِبِ: The one with a predominant urge to urinate or defecate

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they have a strong urge to urinate or defecate during prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on the prayer of the compelled (*al-Mudtir*), this hadith establishes the principle of *khuruj al-waqt* (loss of time) for those with a dominant urge (*ghalib*). It distinguishes this state from a mere need, ruling that the individual need only renew ablution (*wudu*) rather than restarting the entire prayer, thereby balancing ritual purity with the practical necessity of relieving bodily pressure.
